Complete Empirical Research Plan

1. Identification Strategy
Method: Cohort-by-State Triple-Difference (Differences-in-Differences-in-Differences, DDD).

Why:
• We observe two races (Black, White), many birth cohorts (≈1910–1950), and 17 southern states.  
• Relative school resources (Black/White) change sharply across birth cohorts within states but are largely driven by state politics and court rulings, not by contemporaneous earnings of yet-unborn children.  
• DDD removes (i) state-specific macro shocks common to both races, (ii) cohort shocks common to all states, and (iii) race-invariant quality changes.  
• A continuous treatment (the Black/White quality ratio or its change) is interacted with the Black indicator; β estimates how far a one-unit improvement in relative quality raises Black earnings relative to Whites.

Baseline equation (individual i, born in state s, cohort c, observed in Census year t):
ln earnings_isct = α + β (Black_i × RelQual_sc) + γ Black_i  
                 + δ_s + θ_c + ϕ_{s×c} + X′_iλ + ε_isct

δ_s = state-of-birth FE, θ_c = year-of-birth FE, ϕ_{s×c} = state-specific cohort trends.  
X_i: years of schooling, potential experience, Census region of residence, urban dummy.  
Cluster s.e. at state of birth.

2. Treatment and Control
Treatment variable: RelQual_sc – an index (or separate components) of Black school quality relative to White in state s for birth cohort c, normalised so that higher = more resources for Black pupils.

“Treated” units: Black men born in state–cohorts with higher RelQual_sc.

Controls / counterfactual:
• Within-state same-cohort Whites (removes state×cohort shocks).  
• Earlier Black cohorts in the same state (removes time-invariant race bias).  
• Other states (absorbs national trends).

Timing: Exposure dated to birth cohort (or average of birth year + 6–13). No running variable; not an RDD.

3. Key Identifying Assumptions
A1. Parallel-trends-in-absence-of-treatment: Absent quality convergence, Black-White earnings gaps would have evolved similarly across cohorts within a state.  
Plausibility: Major shifts in southern industrial mix, wartime demand, and migration affected both races; DDD removes common shocks. Still needs testing (event-study).

A2. School-quality improvements are predetermined with respect to future cohort-specific labour-market shocks.  
Plausible because changes were driven by court challenges, state legislative responses, and Depression/New Deal finance, not by expectations about 20-year-out labour earnings.

A3. No race-specific selective survival or Census under-enumeration correlated with quality.  
Partially plausible; we will examine cohort-level survival and enumeration rates.

A4. Migration does not differentially bias estimates after controls.  
We will (a) control for current region, (b) replicate on stayers.

4. Threats to Identification & Mitigations
T1. Differential Migration: Higher-quality cohorts may be more likely to leave the South, earning more elsewhere.  
Fix: Add indicators for living outside state-of-birth; run “stayers” sample; show β robust.

T2. Concurrent Race-Specific Policies (e.g., WWII GI Bill, anti-lynching enforcement) that move with quality.  
Fix: Include race-specific state linear trends; control for state×cohort Black veteran rates, lynching decline, manufacturing share.

T3. Measurement Error in School Quality (especially early years).  
Fix: (i) Create an index using PCA to average noisy measures; (ii) instrument each component with its lagged 5-year value (errors are transitory); show attenuation bounds.

5. R Code Outline
```r
# ------------- 0. Packages -------------- #
library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(modelsummary)   # nicer tables

# ------------- 1. Load Data ------------- #
dt <- fread("linked_census_school_quality.csv")  # one row = adult male

# ------------- 2. Variable Construction --#
dt[, black := as.integer(race == "Black")]
# Log earnings, drop zero/negative
dt <- dt[earnings > 0]
dt[, ln_earn := log(earnings)]

# Quality components already merged by state & cohort:
# pt_black, pt_white, term_black, term_white, salary_black, salary_white
# Construct relative quality (higher = better for Blacks)
dt[, rel_pt   := (1/pt_black)/(1/pt_white)]       # teacher per pupil ratio
dt[, rel_term := term_black/term_white]
dt[, rel_sal  := salary_black/salary_white]

# Principal-components index
rel_vars <- c("rel_pt","rel_term","rel_sal")
pc <- prcomp(dt[, ..rel_vars], scale. = TRUE)$x[,1]
dt[, rel_index := as.numeric(scale(pc))]

# Fixed-effect identifiers
dt[, state := factor(state_birth)]
dt[, cohort := factor(year_birth)]
dt[, st_cohort := interaction(state, cohort, drop=TRUE)]

# ------------- 3. Main Regression -------- #
m1 <- feols(ln_earn ~ black*rel_index + educ + exper + exper^2 |
              state + cohort + st_cohort,
            data = dt, cluster = ~state)
etable(m1)

# ------------- 4. Event-study Check ------ #
# Bin cohorts into 5-year groups, interact pre/post with black indicator
dt[, cohort5 := floor(year_birth/5)*5]
m_event <- feols(ln_earn ~ i(cohort5, black, ref = 1920) |
                   state + cohort5 + black + state:cohort5,
                 data = dt, cluster = ~state)
iplot(m_event)   # requires fixest >= 0.10

# ------------- 5. Robustness: Stayers ---- #
m_stay <- feols(ln_earn ~ black*rel_index + educ + exper + exper^2 |
                  state + cohort + st_cohort,
                data = dt[state_birth == state_residence],
                cluster = ~state)
etable(list(Main = m1, Stayers = m_stay))
```

6. Expected Results
Economic theory: Higher school resources raise human-capital accumulation, so β > 0. Historical studies suggest the Black-White earnings gap for southern-born men fell roughly 25–30 log points from the 1910 to 1950 cohorts. I expect about one-third of that (≈8–10 log points) to be explained by relative quality—i.e., a 1 s.d. rise in rel_index boosts Black earnings by ≈4 log points (4%).

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID/DDD)
C1: Parallel pre-trends visually verified ………………… 0.8  
C2: No composition changes (migration, survival) ……… 0.6  
C3: No simultaneous race-specific shocks ……………… 0.6  
C4: Accurate timing of treatment ………………………… 0.9  
C5: SUTVA / no spillovers across states ………………… 0.8  
Average score ≈ 0.74 – credible but still warrants careful robustness work.
